children.text: pāpaṃ na kuryān manasā na vācā kāyena vā kiṃcana sarvaloke /
children.translated_text: One should not commit evil by mind, by speech, or by body — anything at all in the entire world;

children.text: riktaḥ kāmaiḥ smṛtimān saṃprajānaṃ duḥkhaṃ na seveta anarthasaṃhitam // Śag_1.1
children.translated_text: Empty of desires, mindful, clearly comprehending, one should not indulge in suffering connected with purposelessness. // <s>Śag</s> 1.1

children.text: ākhyeyasaṃjñinaḥ satvā ākhyeye 'smin pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Beings are perceivers of what is to be declared, established in this declarable [world];

children.text: ākhyeyam aparijñāya yogam āyānti mṛtyunaḥ // Śag_2.1
children.translated_text: Not having fully understood the declarable, they come under the yoke of death. // <s>Śag</s> 2.1

children.text: ākhyeyaṃ tu parijñāya ākhyātāraṃ na manyate /
children.translated_text: But having fully understood the declarable, one does not conceive of a declarer;

children.text: tad vai na vidyate tasya vadeyur yena taṃ pare // Śag_2.2
children.translated_text: That indeed does not exist for him, by which others might speak of him. // <s>Śag</s> 2.2

children.text: samo viśeṣa uta vāpi hīno yo manyate sa vivadeta tena /
children.translated_text: 'Equal, superior, or even inferior' — whoever thinks thus, he would dispute because of that;

children.text: vidhātraye 'smin na vikampate yaḥ samo viśiṣṭaś ca na tasya bhavati // Śag_2.3
children.translated_text: One who is not shaken by these three modes of comparison — for him neither 'equal' nor 'superior' exists. // <s>Śag</s> 2.3

children.text: ācchidya tṛṣṇām iha nāmarūpe prahāya mānaṃ ca na saṃgam eti /
children.translated_text: Having cut off craving here for name-and-form, having abandoned conceit, one does not come to attachment;

children.text: taṃ śāntadhūmam anighaṃ nirāśaṃ nādrākṣus te devamanuṣyaloke /
children.translated_text: That one of quenched smoke, without affliction, without longing — the gods and humans in the world could not see him,

children.text: iha bāhirataś ca // Śag_2.4
children.translated_text: here or outside. // <s>Śag</s> 2.4

children.text: kāmarāgābhibhūtatvāc cittaṃ me paridahyate /
children.translated_text: My mind is burning, overpowered by passion for sensual desires;

children.text: aṃga me gautama brūhi śāntiṃ tvam anukaṃpayā // Śag_3.1
children.translated_text: O <s>Gautama</s>, please tell me, out of compassion, about peace. // <s>Śag</s> 3.1

children.text: viparyāsena saṃjñānāṃ cittaṃ te paridahyate /
children.translated_text: Your mind is burning through the distortion of perceptions;

children.text: nimittaṃ varjyatāṃ tasmāc chubhaṃ rāgopasaṃhitaṃ // Śag_3.2
children.translated_text: Therefore, the sign (<s>nimitta</s>) connected with passion — the attractive — should be avoided. // <s>Śag</s> 3.2

children.text: aśubhāṃ bhāvaya sadā tvam ekāgraḥ susamāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Cultivate the unattractive (<s>aśubhā</s>) constantly, one-pointed, well-concentrated;

children.text: nirvāpayāśu rāgāgniṃ dahyase mā punaḥ punaḥ // Śag_3.3
children.translated_text: Extinguish quickly the fire of passion — do not be burned again and again. // <s>Śag</s> 3.3

children.text: saṃskārāvaratāṃ paśya duḥkhato 'nātmatas tathā /
children.translated_text: See the formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) as impermanent, as suffering, and likewise as not-self;

children.text: smṛtiṃ kāyagatāṃ kṛtvā nirvedabahulo bhava // Śag_3.4
children.translated_text: Having established mindfulness directed to the body (<s>kāyagatā smṛti</s>), be full of disenchantment. // <s>Śag</s> 3.4

children.text: bhāvyatām animittaṃ ca mānānuśayanāśanaṃ /
children.translated_text: Cultivate the signless (<s>animitta</s>), which destroys the tendency to conceit;

children.text: tato mānābhisamayād duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyasi // Śag_3.5
children.translated_text: Then, through the breaking through of conceit, you will make an end of suffering. // <s>Śag</s> 3.5

children.text: kumārikāpraśnagāthā:
children.translated_text: Verses of the maiden's question (<s>kumārikāpraśnagāthā</s>):

children.text: kathaṃvihārabahulo bhikṣuḥ pañcaughatīrṇas taratīha ṣaṣṭhaṃ /
children.translated_text: How abiding does a <s>bhikṣu</s> cross the five floods and here cross the sixth?

children.text: kathaṃdhyāyī vipulāṃ kāmatṛṣṇāṃ tīrṇo bhavaty apratilabdhayoktraḥ // Śag_4.1
children.translated_text: How meditating does one cross the vast craving for sensual pleasures, having not obtained a yoke? // <s>Śag</s> 4.1

body.text: praśrabdhakāyaḥ suvimuktacitto hy asaṃskurvan smṛtimān akopyaḥ

children.text: ājñāya dharmam avitarkadhyāyī kopaspṛhāstyānadoṣaiḥ viyuktaḥ // Śag_4.2
children.translated_text: Having known the <s>Dharma</s>, meditating without discursive thought, free from the faults of anger, desire, and sloth. // <s>Śag</s> 4.2

children.text: evaṃvihārabahulo bhikṣuḥ pañcaughatīrṇas taratīha ṣaṣṭhaṃ /
children.translated_text: Thus abiding, the <s>bhikṣu</s> crosses the five floods and here crosses the sixth;

children.text: evaṃdhyāyī vipulāṃ kāmatṛṣṇāṃ tīrṇo bhavaty apratilabdhayoktraḥ // Śag_4.3
children.translated_text: Thus meditating, one crosses the vast craving for sensual pleasures, having not obtained a yoke. // <s>Śag</s> 4.3

body.translated_text: With body tranquil, well-liberated in mind, not fabricating, mindful, unshakable,

children.text: nityotrasto hy ayaṃ loko nityodvignā iyaṃ prajā /
children.translated_text: This world is constantly frightened, this humanity is constantly anxious,

children.text: anutpanneṣu duḥkheṣu samutpanneṣu vā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whether sufferings have not yet arisen or have already arisen —

children.text: yadi kiṃcid anutrastaṃ pṛṣṭa ācakṣva tan mama // Śag_5.1
children.translated_text: If there is anything not frightening, when asked, tell me that. // <s>Śag</s> 5.1

children.text: nānyatra jñānatapaso nānyatrendriyanigrahāt /
children.translated_text: I see no liberation other than through knowledge and austerity, other than through sense-restraint,

children.text: nānyatra sarvasaṃtyāgān mokṣaṃ paśyāmi devate // Śag_5.2
children.translated_text: Other than through the renunciation of all, O deity. // <s>Śag</s> 5.2

children.text: cirasya bata paśyāmi brāhmaṇaṃ parinirvṛtaṃ /
children.translated_text: At long last I see a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has attained complete <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: sarvavairabhayātītaṃ tīrṇaṃ loke viṣaktikām // Śag_5.3
children.translated_text: Who has gone beyond all enmity and fear, who has crossed over attachment in the world. // <s>Śag</s> 5.3

children.text: kenābhivarṇā janatā praṇītā mārgaś ca nairyāṇikataḥ prayuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: By what has humanity been described as excellent, and the path been set as leading out?

children.text: kutra sthitaḥ kutra ca śikṣamāṇo nāyaṃ martyaḥ paralokād bibheti // Śag_6.1
children.translated_text: Established in what, and training in what, does this mortal not fear the other world? // <s>Śag</s> 6.1

children.text: yaḥ śīlavāñ jñānavān bhāvitātmā samāhitaḥ smṛtimān ṛjugataś ca /
children.translated_text: One who is endowed with morality, possessed of knowledge, with cultivated self, concentrated, mindful, and going straight —

children.text: sarve 'sya śokajvarathāḥ prahīṇāḥ samyaksmṛto yasya cittaṃ vimuktaṃ // Śag_6.2
children.translated_text: All his sorrows and fevers are abandoned; whose mind is liberated, properly mindful. // <s>Śag</s> 6.2

children.text: tenābhivarṇā janatā praṇītā mārgaś ca nairyāṇikataḥ prayuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: By that has humanity been described as excellent, and the path been set as leading out;

children.text: atra sthitaḥ atra ca śikṣamāṇo nāyaṃ martyaḥ paralokād bibheti // Śag_6.3
children.translated_text: Established in that, and training in that, this mortal does not fear the other world. // <s>Śag</s> 6.3

children.text: kathaṃ yaśasvī bhavati kathaṃ bhavati bhogavān /
children.translated_text: How does one become famous? How does one become wealthy?

children.text: kathaṃ kīrtim avāpnoti kathaṃ mitrāṇi vindati // Śag_7.1
children.translated_text: How does one attain renown? How does one find friends? // <s>Śag</s> 7.1

children.text: śīlād yaśasvī bhavati dānād bhavati bhogavān /
children.translated_text: Through morality one becomes famous, through generosity one becomes wealthy;

children.text: satyena kīrtim āpnoti dadan mitrāṇi vindati // Śag_7.2
children.translated_text: Through truthfulness one attains renown; by giving, one finds friends. // <s>Śag</s> 7.2

children.text: kutaḥ sarā nivartante kutra vartma na vartate /
children.translated_text: Whence do the streams turn back? Where does the path not proceed?

children.text: kutra duḥkhasukhaṃ loke niḥśeṣam uparudhyate // Śag_8.1
children.translated_text: Where are suffering and happiness in the world entirely cut off? // <s>Śag</s> 8.1

children.text: cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ tathā ghrāṇaṃ jihvā kāyo manas tathā /
children.translated_text: The eye, the ear, likewise the nose, the tongue, the body, and likewise the mind —

children.text: yatra nāma ca rūpaṃ ca niḥśeṣam uparuhyate // Śag_8.2
children.translated_text: Where name and form are entirely cut off — // <s>Śag</s> 8.2

children.text: tataḥ sarā nivartante tatra vartma na vartate /
children.translated_text: From there the streams turn back, there the path does not proceed;

children.text: tatra duḥkhasukhaṃ loke niḥśeṣam uparudhyate // Śag_8.3
children.translated_text: There suffering and happiness in the world are entirely cut off. // <s>Śag</s> 8.3

children.text: kena svid oghaṃ tarati kenottarati cārṇavaṃ /
children.translated_text: By what does one cross the flood? By what does one cross the ocean?

children.text: duḥkhaṃ tyajati kena svit kena svit pariśudhyati // Śag_9.1
children.translated_text: By what does one abandon suffering? By what is one purified? // <s>Śag</s> 9.1

children.text: śraddhayā tarati hy ogham apramādena cārṇavaṃ /
children.translated_text: By faith one crosses the flood, by diligence one crosses the ocean;

children.text: vīryeṇa duḥkhaṃ tyajati prajñayā pariśudhyati // Śag_9.2
children.translated_text: By vigor one abandons suffering, by wisdom one is purified. // <s>Śag</s> 9.2

children.text: ka etam oghaṃ tarati rātriṃdivam atandritaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who crosses this flood, tireless day and night?

children.text: anālambe 'pratiṣṭhe ca ko gaṃbhīre na sīdati // Śag_10.1
children.translated_text: Who does not sink in the deep, without support and without footing? // <s>Śag</s> 10.1

children.text: sarvataḥ śīlasaṃpannaḥ prajñāvān susamāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: One endowed with morality in every way, wise, well-concentrated,

children.text: adhyātmacintī smṛtimāṃs taratīmaṃ sudustaraṃ // Śag_10.2
children.translated_text: Contemplating the inner self, mindful — he crosses this most difficult to cross. // <s>Śag</s> 10.2

children.text: viraktaḥ kāmasaṃjñābhyo rūpasaṃyojanātigaḥ /
children.translated_text: Dispassionate toward perceptions of sensual desire, gone beyond the fetters of form —

children.text: anālambe 'pratiṣṭhe ca sa gaṃbhīre na sīdati // Śag_10.3
children.translated_text: He does not sink in the deep, without support and without footing. // <s>Śag</s> 10.3

children.text: rāgadveṣau bhagavan kinnidānāv aratiratī romaharṣaḥ kuto 'yam /
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhagavān</s>, what is the cause of passion and hatred? From where arise aversion, delight, and horripilation?

children.text: kutaḥsamutthāś ca mano vitarkāḥ kumārakā dhātrīm ivāśrayante // Śag_11.1
children.translated_text: From where do the mind's thoughts arise, resting [upon it] as boys upon a nurse? // <s>Śag</s> 11.1

children.text: snehajā ātmasaṃbhūtā nyagrodhaskandhakā yathā /
children.translated_text: Born from affection, arisen from the self, like the trunk of a banyan tree;

children.text: pṛthagviṣaktāḥ kāmeṣu mālutā vā latā vane // Śag_11.2
children.translated_text: Variously attached to desires, like creepers in a forest [clinging to trees]. // <s>Śag</s> 11.2

children.text: rāgaś ca dveṣaś ca itonidānāv aratiratī romaharṣaḥ ito 'yaṃ /
children.translated_text: Passion and hatred have their cause from here; aversion, delight, and horripilation [arise] from here;

children.text: itaḥsamutthāś ca mano vitarkāḥ kumārakā dhātrīm ivāśrayante // Śag_11.3
children.translated_text: The mind's thoughts arise from here, resting as boys upon a nurse. // <s>Śag</s> 11.3

children.text: ye tān prajānanti yatonidānāṃs te tāṃ janā yakṣa vinodayanti /
children.translated_text: Those who understand them and their cause — those people, O <s>yakṣa</s>, dispel them;

children.text: ta arṇavaṃ saṃpratarantīhaugham atīrṇapūrvam apunarbhavāya // Śag_11.4
children.translated_text: They cross this ocean-flood, never crossed before, for the sake of non-return to existence. // <s>Śag</s> 11.4

children.text: kāryam etad brāhmaṇena prahāṇam akilāsinā /
children.translated_text: This must be done by a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — this abandoning, tirelessly —

children.text: kāmānāṃ viprahāṇārthaṃ na hi kāṃkṣaty asau bhavaṃ // Śag_12.1
children.translated_text: For the purpose of abandoning desires; for he does not long for existence. // <s>Śag</s> 12.1

body.text: sa kāryaṃ brāhmaṇasyāsti kṛtārtho brāhmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ // Śag_12.2
body.translated_text: He has the task of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> accomplished; a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is remembered as one who has fulfilled his purpose. // <s>Śag</s> 12.2

children.text: yāvan na gādhaṃ labhate na tīram āyūhate sarvagātraiḥ sa tāvat /
children.translated_text: As long as one finds neither ford nor shore, one struggles with all limbs;

children.text: tīraṃ tu labdhveha saṃtiṣṭhati sthale nāyūhate pāragato nirucyate // Śag_12.3
children.translated_text: But having found the shore here, one stands on solid ground — one no longer struggles — one is called 'gone to the far shore.' // <s>Śag</s> 12.3

children.text: eṣopamā dāmale brāhmaṇasya kṣīṇāsravo yo nipako dhyānalābhī /
children.translated_text: This is the simile, O <s>Dāmale</s>, for the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> whose outflows (<s>āsravas</s>) are destroyed, who is prudent, who has attained <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption);

children.text: sarve 'sya śokajvarathāḥ prahīṇāḥ samyaksmṛto yasya cittaṃ vimuktam // Śag_12.4
children.translated_text: All his sorrows and fevers are abandoned — one who is properly mindful, whose mind is liberated. // <s>Śag</s> 12.4

body.text:
geya:
bhikṣo bhikṣo ogham atārṣīḥ /
āma devate /
anālambe 'pratiṣṭhe ogham atārṣīḥ /
āma devate /
yathā kathaṃ tvaṃ bhikṣo anālambe apratiṣṭhe ogham atārṣīḥ /
yathā yathāhaṃ devate āyūhāmi tathā tathā saṃsīdāmi / yathā yathā saṃsīdāmi tathā tathā saṃtiṣṭhe / yathā yathā saṃtiṣṭhe tathā tathā uhye / yathā yathāhaṃ devate nāyūhāmi tathā tathā na saṃsīdāmīti vistareṇa śuklapakṣo veditavya

children.text: ḥ
children.translated_text: [continued]

body.translated_text:
<s>Geya</s> (song):
'O <s>bhikṣu</s>, <s>bhikṣu</s>, have you crossed the flood?'
'Yes, O deity.'
'Without support, without footing, have you crossed the flood?'
'Yes, O deity.'
'How then, O <s>bhikṣu</s>, have you crossed the flood without support and without footing?'
'Whenever I struggle, O deity, then I sink; whenever I sink, then I stand; whenever I stand, then I am carried away. Whenever I do not struggle, O deity, then I do not sink' — the bright half [of the teaching] is to be understood in detail.

children.text: kumārikāpraśnagāthā:
children.translated_text: Verses of the maiden's question (<s>kumārikāpraśnagāthā</s>):

children.text: eko 'raṇye prasṛto dhyāyase tvaṃ vittād vihīna uta vā prārthayānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alone in the forest you meditate, wandering — deprived of wealth, or seeking?

children.text: grāmasya vā kiṃcanāgo nv akārṣīḥ kasmāj janena na karoṣi sakhyaṃ
children.translated_text: Or have you done some wrong to the village? Why do you not make friendship with people —

children.text: sakhyaṃ na saṃvidyate kena cit tava // Śag_14.1
children.translated_text: Friendship is not found with anyone for you? // <s>Śag</s> 14.1

children.text: arthāprāptyā hṛdayasyeha śāntir jitveha senāṃ priyaśātarūpaṃ /
children.translated_text: Through the non-attainment of [material] things, there is peace of the heart here; having conquered the army of pleasant and beautiful forms,

children.text: eko dhyāyī sukham asmy anvabhotsaṃ tasmād janena na karomi sakhyaṃ
children.translated_text: Meditating alone, I have experienced happiness; therefore I do not make friendship with people —

children.text: sakhyaṃ na saṃvidyate kena cid mama // Śag_14.2
children.translated_text: Friendship is not found with anyone for me. // <s>Śag</s> 14.2

children.text: anityā bata saṃskārā utpādavyayadharmiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Impermanent indeed are conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>), subject to arising and passing away;

children.text: utpadya hi nirudhyante teṣāṃ vyupaśamaḥ sukham // Śag_15 (cf. Uv 1.3)
children.translated_text: Having arisen, they cease — their pacification is happiness. // <s>Śag</s> 15 (cf. <s>Uv</s> 1.3)

body.text:
apramādo 'mṛtapadaṃ pramādo mṛtyunaḥ padaṃ /
apramattā na mriyante pramattās tu sadā mṛtā

children.text: ḥ
children.translated_text: [continued]

children.text: vitarkapramathitasya dehinas tīvrarāgasya śubhānudarśinaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the embodied being shaken by discursive thoughts, of intense passion, seeing the attractive —

children.text: bhūyas tṛṣṇā vivardhate sā gāḍhīkurute 'sya bandhanaṃ // Śag_17 (cf. Uv 3.1)
children.translated_text: Craving increases further; it tightens the bonds upon him. // <s>Śag</s> 17 (cf. <s>Uv</s> 3.1)

children.text: dharmasthaṃ śīlasaṃpannaṃ hrīmantaṃ satyavādinaṃ /
children.translated_text: One established in <s>Dharma</s>, endowed with morality, possessed of modesty, speaking truth —

children.text: ātmanaḥ priyakartāraṃ taṃ janaḥ kurute priyaṃ // Śag_18 (cf. Uv 5.24)
children.translated_text: The one who does what is dear to the self — that person people hold dear. // <s>Śag</s> 18 (cf. <s>Uv</s> 5.24)

children.text: yat pareṣūpanidhyāyet karma dṛṣṭveha pāpakam /
children.translated_text: What evil action one has seen in others,

children.text: ātmanā tan na kurvīta karmabaddho hi pāpakaḥ // Śag_19 (cf. Uv 9.6)
children.translated_text: That one should not do oneself; for the evildoer is bound by [evil] action. // <s>Śag</s> 19 (cf. <s>Uv</s> 9.6)

children.text: subhāṣitaṃ hy uttamam āhur āryāḥ priyaṃ vaden nāpriyaṃ tad dvitīyaṃ /
children.translated_text: Noble ones say well-spoken speech is the highest; speak the pleasant, not the unpleasant — that is the second;

children.text: satyaṃ vaden nānṛtaṃ tat tṛtīyaṃ dharmaṃ vaden nādharmaṃ tat caturtham // Śag_20 (cf. Uv 8.11)
children.translated_text: Speak the true, not the false — that is the third; speak the <s>Dharma</s>, not the non-<s>Dharma</s> — that is the fourth. // <s>Śag</s> 20 (cf. <s>Uv</s> 8.11)

children.text: śraddhātha hrīḥ śīlam athāpi dānaṃ dharmā ime satpuruṣapraśastāḥ /
children.translated_text: Faith, modesty, morality, and also generosity — these <s>dharmas</s> are praised by the virtuous;

children.text: etaṃ hi mārgaṃ divigaṃ vadanti etena vai gacchati devalokam // Śag_21 (cf. Uv 10.1)
children.translated_text: This path they call leading to heaven — by this indeed one goes to the world of the gods. // <s>Śag</s> 21 (cf. <s>Uv</s> 10.1)

children.text: śrutvā dharmaṃ vijānāti śrutvā pāpān nivartate /
children.translated_text: Having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, one understands; having heard, one turns away from evil;

children.text: śrutvā anarthaṃ tyajati śrutvā prāpnoti nirvṛtim // Śag_22 (cf. Uv 22.6)
children.translated_text: having heard, one abandons what is harmful; having heard, one attains <s>nirvṛti</s> (peace). // <s>Śag</s> 22 //

children.text: ākāśasamo na lipyate indrakīlapratimo na kaṃpate /
children.translated_text: Like space, he is not stained; like <s>Indra</s>'s pillar, he does not tremble;

children.text: hrada iva samupetakardame saṃsāre ramate na paṇḍitaḥ // Śag_23 (cf. Uv 17.12)
children.translated_text: like [one facing] a lake filled with mud, the wise one does not delight in <s>saṃsāra</s>. // <s>Śag</s> 23 //

children.text: ye rūpeṇa pramiṇvanti māṃ ghoṣeṇānuyānti ca /
children.translated_text: Those who judge me by form or follow me by sound —

children.text: cchandarāgavaśopetā na mā jānanti te janāḥ // Śag_24.1 (cf. Uv 22.12)
children.translated_text: overcome by the power of desire and passion, those people do not know me. // <s>Śag</s> 24.1 //

children.text: adhyātmaṃ ca vijānāti bahirdhā ca na paśyati /
children.translated_text: One who understands the inner (<s>adhyātma</s>) but does not see the outer —

children.text: adhyātmaphaladarśī yaḥ sa vai ghoṣeṇa nīyate // Śag_24.2 (cf. Uv 22.13)
children.translated_text: one who sees only the fruit of the inner, he indeed is led by sound. // <s>Śag</s> 24.2 //

children.text: adhyātmaṃ ca na jānāti bahirdhā ca vipaśyati /
children.translated_text: One who does not know the inner but sees the outer —

children.text: bahirdhāphaladarśī yaḥ so 'pi ghoṣeṇa nīyate // Śag_24.3 (cf. Uv 22.14)
children.translated_text: one who sees only the fruit of the outer, he too is led by sound. // <s>Śag</s> 24.3 //

children.text: adhyātmaṃ ca na jānāti bahirdhā ca na paśyati /
children.translated_text: One who neither knows the inner nor sees the outer —

children.text: samantāvaraṇo bālaḥ so 'pi ghoṣeṇa nīyate // Śag_24.4 (cf. Uv 22.15)
children.translated_text: a fool obstructed on all sides, he too is led by sound. // <s>Śag</s> 24.4 //

children.text: adhyātmaṃ ca vijānāti bahirdhā ca vipaśyati /
children.translated_text: One who understands the inner and sees the outer —

children.text: dhīro niḥsaraṇaprajño na sa ghoṣeṇa nīyate // Śag_24.5 (cf. Uv 22.16)
children.translated_text: the wise one, with insight into escape (<s>niḥsaraṇa</s>), he is not led by sound. // <s>Śag</s> 24.5 //

body.translated_text: Heedfulness (<s>apramāda</s>) is the state of the deathless; heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>) is the state of death; the heedful do not die, but the heedless are as if always dead.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe adhipatau rājñi rajyamāne rajasvalaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the sixth ruler, the king [i.e., the mind], is attached, one becomes passion-stained;

children.text: arajasy arajā bhavati rakto bālo nirucyate // Śag_25 (cf. Uv 16.22)
children.translated_text: in the passionless [state], one becomes free from passion; the attached fool is thus declared. // <s>Śag</s> 25 //

children.text: nagaram asthiprākāraṃ snāyumāṃsānulepanaṃ /
children.translated_text: A city with walls of bone, plastered with sinew and flesh —

children.text: yatra rāgaś ca dveṣaś ca māno mrakṣaś ca gāhate // Śag_26 (cf. Uv 16.23)
children.translated_text: where passion, hatred, pride, and hypocrisy abide. // <s>Śag</s> 26 //

children.text: kūrmaḥ svake 'ṅgāni yathā kapāle bhikṣur nidadhyān manaso vitarkāni /
children.translated_text: Just as a tortoise [withdraws] its limbs into its shell, so should a <s>bhikṣu</s> withdraw the thoughts of the mind;

children.text: aniśrito 'nyān aviheṭhamānaḥ parinirvṛto nāpavadeta kaṃ cit // Śag_27 (cf. Uv 26.1)
children.translated_text: not dependent on others, not harming [anyone], fully at peace, one should not speak ill of anyone. // <s>Śag</s> 27 //

children.text: tulyam atulyaṃ ca saṃbhavaṃ bhavasaṃskāram avāsṛjan muniḥ /
children.translated_text: Having cast off both the equal and unequal [aspects of] existence, [and] the formations of becoming, the <s>muni</s> (sage),

children.text: adhyātmarataḥ samāhita abhinat kośam ivāṇḍasaṃbhavaḥ // Śag_28 (cf. Uv 26.30)
children.translated_text: delighting inwardly, concentrated, broke through the shell like one born from an egg. // <s>Śag</s> 28 //

children.text: nāsti kāmasamaḥ paṃko nāsti dveṣasamo grahaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no mire like desire, no demon like hatred,

children.text: nāsti mohasamaṃ jālaṃ nāsti tṛṣṇāsamā nadī // Śag_29 (cf. Uv 29.37)
children.translated_text: no net like delusion, no river like craving. // <s>Śag</s> 29 //

children.text: ākāśe vai padaṃ nāsti śramaṇo nāsti bāhyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no footprint in the sky; there is no <s>śramaṇa</s> (renunciant) outside [the teaching];

children.text: prapañcābhiratā bālā niṣprapañcās tathāgatāḥ // Śag_30 (cf. Uv 29.38)
children.translated_text: fools delight in <s>prapañca</s> (proliferation); the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are free from proliferation. // <s>Śag</s> 30 //

body.text: sthitiḥ prapaṃcāś ca na santi yasya yaḥ sa

children.text: ṃ
children.translated_text: the

children.text: dānaṃ parighaṃ cātivṛttaḥ /
children.translated_text: bonds and the bar —

children.text: taṃ nistṛṣṇaṃ muniṃ carantaṃ na vijānāti sadevako 'pi lokaḥ // Śag_31 (cf. Uv 29.51)
children.translated_text: that thirstless <s>muni</s> (sage), wandering, even the world with its gods does not know. // <s>Śag</s> 31 //

children.text:
yasya vitarkā vidhūpitā adhyātmam avikalpitā aśeṣaṃ /
saṃgaṃ so 'tītya rūpasaṃjñā
children.translated_text: Whose thoughts are dispersed, who is inwardly free from conceptual proliferation entirely — having gone beyond attachment and the perception of form,

children.text: ṃ
caturyogāpagato na jātim eti // Śag_32 (cf. Uv 29.56)
children.translated_text: freed from the four yokes, he does not come to birth. // <s>Śag</s> 32 //

children.text: dadataḥ puṇyaṃ pravardhate vairaṃ saṃyamato na cīyate /
children.translated_text: Through giving, merit increases; through self-restraint, enmity does not accumulate;

children.text: kuśalī prajahāti pāpakaṃ kleśānāṃ kṣayatas tu nirvṛtaḥ // Śag_33 (cf. Uv 28.2)
children.translated_text: the skilled one abandons evil; through the destruction of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), one is at peace. // <s>Śag</s> 33 //

children.text: sarvapāpasyākaraṇaṃ kuśalasyopasaṃpadā /
children.translated_text: The non-doing of all evil, the cultivation of what is wholesome,

children.text: svacittaparyavadamanam etaṃ buddhānuśāsanaṃ // Śag_34 (cf. Uv 28.1)
children.translated_text: the purification of one's own mind — this is the teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s>. // <s>Śag</s> 34 //

children.text: durnigrahasya laghuno yatrakāmanipātinaḥ /
children.translated_text: The taming of the mind — which is hard to restrain, fickle, alighting wherever it pleases —

children.text: cittasya dāmanaṃ sādhu cittaṃ dāntaṃ sukhāvaham // Śag_35 (cf. Uv 31.1)
children.translated_text: is good; a tamed mind brings happiness. // <s>Śag</s> 35 //

children.text: cittanimittasya kovidaḥ pravivekasya ca vindate rasaṃ /
children.translated_text: One skilled in the sign of the mind finds delight in solitude;

children.text: dhyāyī nipakaḥ pratismṛto bhuṃkte prītisukhaṃ nirāmiṣaṃ // Śag_36 (cf. Uv 31.51)
children.translated_text: meditating, prudent, mindful, one enjoys the bliss of joy that is without worldly attachment. // <s>Śag</s> 36 //

children.text:
aśilpajīvī laghur ātmakāmo jitendriyaḥ sarvato vipramuktaḥ /
anokasārī hy amamo nirāśaḥ kāmān prahāyaikacaro yas sa bhikṣu
children.translated_text: Living without craft, light, self-possessed, with senses conquered, released on all sides, homeless, without attachment, without desire — one who, having abandoned sensual pleasures, wanders alone, that one is a <s>bhikṣu</s>

children.text: ḥ

// Śag_37 (cf. Uv 32.5)
dūraṃga
children.translated_text: // <s>Śag</s> 37 // Far-wandering,

children.text: ma
m ekacaram aśarīraṃ guhāśayaṃ /
children.translated_text: solitary, bodiless, dwelling in the cave [of the heart] —

children.text: damayati durdamaṃ cittaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ taṃ bravīmy ahaṃ // Śag_38 (cf. Uv 33.55)
children.translated_text: one who tames the hard-to-tame mind, that one I call a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. // <s>Śag</s> 38 //

body.translated_text: For whom there is no fixed abode and no proliferations, who has gone beyond

children.text: pārāyaṇeṣv ajitapraśnaḥ:
children.translated_text: In the <s>Pārāyaṇa</s> [section], the question of <s>Ajita</s>:

children.text: kenāyaṃ nivṛto lokaḥ kenāyaṃ na prakāśate /
children.translated_text: 'By what is this world enveloped? By what does it not shine?

children.text: kiṃ cābhilepanaṃ brūṣe kiṃ ca tasya mahad bhayam // Śag_39.1
children.translated_text: What do you call its smearing? What is its great fear?' // <s>Śag</s> 39.1 //

children.text: avidyānivṛto lokaḥ pramādān na prakāśate /
children.translated_text: 'By <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is this world enveloped; by heedlessness it does not shine;

children.text: jalpābhilepanaṃ brūmi duḥkhaṃ tasya mahad bhayaṃ // Śag_39.2
children.translated_text: idle talk I call its smearing; <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) is its great fear.' // <s>Śag</s> 39.2 //

children.text: sravanti sarvataḥ srotāḥ srotasāṃ kiṃ nivāraṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'The currents flow everywhere — what is the restraint of the currents?

children.text: srotasāṃ saṃvaraṃ brūhi kena srotaḥ pidhīyate // Śag_39.3
children.translated_text: Tell me the restraint of the currents — by what is the current dammed?' // <s>Śag</s> 39.3 //

children.text: yāni srotāṃsi lokasya smṛtiḥ teṣāṃ nivāraṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever currents there are in the world — <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is their restraint;

children.text: srotasāṃ saṃvaraṃ brūmi prajñayā hi pidhīyate // Śag_39.4
children.translated_text: the restraint of the currents I declare — by <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) indeed are they dammed.' // <s>Śag</s> 39.4 //

children.text: prajñāyāś ca smṛteś caiva nāmarūpasya sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), and of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) entirely —

children.text: ācakṣva pṛṣṭa etan me kutraitad uparudhyate // Śag_39.5
children.translated_text: tell me, I ask you this: where does all this cease?' // <s>Śag</s> 39.5 //

children.text: prajñā caiva smṛtiś caiva nāmarūpaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), and <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) entirely —

children.text: vijñānasya nirodhād dhi atraitad uparudhyate // Śag_39.6
children.translated_text: through the cessation of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) indeed, here all this ceases.' // <s>Śag</s> 39.6 //

children.text: kathaṃ smṛtasya carato vijñānam uparudhyate /
children.translated_text: 'How, for one who is mindful and practicing, does <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) cease?

children.text: ācakṣva pṛṣṭa etan me yathātatham asaṃśayaḥ // Śag_39.7
children.translated_text: Tell me, I ask you this, as it truly is, without doubt.' // <s>Śag</s> 39.7 //

children.text: adhyātaṃ ca bahirdhā ca vedanāṃ nābhinandataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For one who does not delight in <s>vedanā</s> (feelings), whether internal or external —

children.text: evaṃ smṛtasya carato vijñānam uparudhyate // Śag_39.8
children.translated_text: for one who is thus mindful and practicing, <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) ceases.' // <s>Śag</s> 39.8 //

body.text: ye ca saṃkhyātadharmāṇo ye ca śaikṣāḥ pṛ

children.text: tha
gvidhāḥ /
children.translated_text: various kinds —

children.text: teṣāṃ me nipakasyeryāṃ pṛṣṭaḥ prabrūhi mārṣa // Śag_39.9
children.translated_text: their conduct, being prudent — tell me when asked, O venerable sir.' // <s>Śag</s> 39.9 //

children.text: kāmeṣu nābhigṛdhyeta manasānāvilo bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'One should not be greedy for sensual pleasures; the mind should be unclouded;

children.text: kuśalaḥ sarvadharmeṣu smṛto bhikṣuḥ parivrajet // Śag_39.10
children.translated_text: skilled in all <s>dharmas</s>, mindful, a <s>bhikṣu</s> should wander forth.' // <s>Śag</s> 39.10 //

body.translated_text: 'Those who have enumerated the <s>dharmas</s>, and those who are <s>śaikṣas</s> (learners) of

children.text: arthavargīyeṣu kāmān ārabhya gāthā:
children.translated_text: In the <s>Arthavargīya</s> [section], verses concerning <s>kāma</s> (desires):

children.text: kāmān kāmāyamānasya tasya cet tat samṛdhyati /
children.translated_text: For one who desires desires, if that [desire] is fulfilled,

children.text: addhā prītamanā bhavati labdhvā martyo yad īpsitaṃ // Śag_40.1
children.translated_text: the mortal indeed becomes glad-minded, having obtained what was wished for. // <s>Śag</s> 40.1 //

children.text: tasya cet kāmāyamānasya chandajātasya jaṃtunaḥ /
children.translated_text: But if for that being who desires, in whom longing has arisen,

children.text: te kāmāḥ parihīyaṃte śalyaviddha iva rūpyate // Śag_40.2
children.translated_text: those desires fail, he suffers as if pierced by a dart. // <s>Śag</s> 40.2 //

children.text: yaḥ kāmāṃ parivarjayati sarpasyeva śirāt padaṃ /
children.translated_text: One who avoids desires, as [one avoids placing] a foot on a serpent's head,

children.text: sa imāṃ viṣaktikāṃ loke smṛtaḥ samativartate // Śag_40.3
children.translated_text: that mindful one overcomes this clinging in the world. // <s>Śag</s> 40.3 //

children.text: kṣetravastuhiraṇ@yaṃ ca gavāśvamaṇikuṇḍalaṃ /
children.translated_text: Fields, property, gold, cattle, horses, jewels, earrings,

children.text: striyo dāsān pṛthakkāmān yo naro hy abhigṛdhyati // Śag_40.4
children.translated_text: women, servants, and various desires — the man who craves for these — // <s>Śag</s> 40.4 //

body.text: abalaṃ vā balīyāṃso mṛdnaṃty enaṃ parisravā

children.text: ḥ
children.translated_text: him

children.text: tata enaṃ duḥkham anveti bhinnāṃ nāvam ivodakaṃ // Śag_40.5
children.translated_text: then suffering follows him, as water [enters] a broken boat. // <s>Śag</s> 40.5 //

children.text: yasya tv etat samucchinnaṃ tālamastakavad dhataṃ /
children.translated_text: But for one who has completely cut this off, destroyed like the crown of a palm tree —

children.text: śokās tasya nivartante udabindur iva puṣkarāt // Śag_40.6 (cf. Uv 10.13ab und 3.10cd)
children.translated_text: sorrows turn away from him, like a water-drop from a lotus. // <s>Śag</s> 40.6 //

body.translated_text: the powerless one, the strong [afflictions] crush him, the outflows overwhelm

children.text: bhadraikarāgāthā (bhadragarātrīya, bhadrakarātriya):
children.translated_text: <s>Bhadraika-rāga-gāthā</s> (Verses on the Auspicious Single Night):

children.text: atītaṃ nānvāgamayen na pratikāṃkṣed anāgataṃ /
children.translated_text: One should not run after the past, nor long for the future;

children.text: pratyutpannāś ca ye dharmās tatra tatra vipaśyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: whatever <s>dharmas</s> are present, one should observe them there and there;

children.text: asaṃhāryam asaṃkṣobhyaṃ tad vidvān anubṛṃhayet // Śag_41.1
children.translated_text: that which is irremovable and unshakable — the wise one should cultivate that. // <s>Śag</s> 41.1 //
